subject: Request: EU-only model binding + no-fallback for regulated Medisys deployment
messages:
From: Veronica Stead <veronica.stead@medisys.ai>
To: camila_reyes@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@medisys.ai
Date: Mon, 8 Mar 2027 13:02:00 +0000
Subject: Deployment constraints / model binding request

Hi Camila —

Thanks for the demo last week. Legal and security reviewed the integration and we have two hard constraints before procurement will sign: 

1) All inference for Medisys EU production traffic must be pinned to a single model variant (model-v2-quant) with no automatic fallback to other variants.
2) All traffic must be routed to EU-only infrastructure (no cross-region routing).

Because we process regulated patient summaries, any fallback behavior that routes outside EU or to model variants with different quantization/profile is a contractual no-go. I attached the compliance spreadsheet with the exact asks.

Question: can Redwood enforce a “hard model bind” + region lock at the route level (so even under capacity pressure we do not fallback)? If not possible, we need to understand technical mitigations and the operational SLA impact.

We’re trying to close by end of quarter — can you share feasibility and a rough ETA?

Thanks,
Veronica Stead
Head of Platform Security
Medisys Health

Attachments: medisys-eu-requirements.xlsx, SOC2-evidence-request.pdf

- Expose a route-level flag that disables fallback (no-fallback==true) and enforces region-only routing.

Notes: this needs product + engineering alignment — if we need a short-term manual process (ops pinning) that’s fine but call out risk.

Thanks — I’d like a one-paragraph feasibility note + bullet timeline by EOD tomorrow. I’ll reply to Veronica after we sync.

— Camila
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
To: camila_reyes@redwood.ai, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: veronica.stead@medisys.ai
Date: Tue, 9 Mar 2027 09:11:00 +00:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Deployment constraints / model binding request

Camila / team — summary of technical feasibility and risks: 

Short answer: we can implement a hard model bind + region lock but there are trade-offs and implementation choices. Options below with impact and rough ETA.

1) Configuration-only enforcement (fast) — ETA: 1 week dev + 2 days ops playbook
   - Mechanism: add route config flags: enforce_region=\"eu\" and allow_fallback=false.
   - Behavior: runtime rejects/queues any request that would be routed out of region or to a different model variant.
   - Trade-offs: Under saturated capacity this will cause request rejections or increased latency as we throttle; no automatic fallback reduces availability. We can add prioritized queueing for the route but it's best-effort.

2) Runtime kernel change + hard pin (medium) — ETA: 4–6 weeks
   - Mechanism: extend router to treat pinned model variants as non-elastic: do not consider compatible substitutes when scheduling across pools.
   - Trade-offs: more invasive; requires changes to autoscaler and cold-start paths to ensure reserved capacity for pinned variants. Provides predictable correctness but needs capacity commitment (Dedicated or reserved pools).

3) Hybrid (recommended short-term -> long-term)
   - Short-term: option #1 + ops playbook + explicit SLA exception in contract (Medisys can accept slower tails or rejections for a week while we provision reserved capacity).
   - Long-term: option #2 with reserved pools and dashboard warnings.

Additional notes:
- Quantized variant (model-v2-quant) compatibility: OK for inference, but we must add a verification step in onboarding to ensure the exact artifact (hash) is used.
- Observability: product will need to surface real-time route-level rejections and a fallback-disabled flag in the Console (I can add trace points).
- Security: region lock requires strong enforcement of network egress rules; infra will need to gate any cross-region failover.

Risks: increased cost if customer needs reserved capacity; possible SLA exceptions for availability. If Medisys requires no-fallback under all circumstances, we should require a capacity commitment.

If this aligns, I can scope a short RFC for option #1 by tomorrow and a delivery plan for #2.

— Rishi
Engineering Manager, Serving Runtime
From: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai

Thanks Rishi — this is helpful. Product / Sales notes (short):

- Business ask: Medisys requires contract language that guarantees model-binding + EU-only processing without automated fallback. They accept an SLA exception (availability will be lower) if we commit to reserved capacity.
- Ask to Eng: please produce the RFC for option #1 (configuration) and a clear cost delta for reserved capacity (monthly). Also please list the exact console UX changes we need to surface (warning banners, per-route toggle, rejection metrics).
- Legal/Compliance: I’ll loop in Legal for contract language (we need indemnities and clear outage/availability terms).

Camila — if Ops can temporarily pin the route manually while Eng implements option #1, that may buy time. We should plan a short Exec summary for Medisys showing trade-offs and proposed timeline (short-term: ops pinning + config flag; long-term: reserved pool + hard pin).

I can draft the customer-facing note after you approve the short-term plan.

— Lauren
VP, Product Management
From: camila_reyes@redwood.ai

Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, procurement@medisys.ai

Subject: Re: Deployment constraints / model binding request

Hi Veronica — thanks for the clarity and the spreadsheet (attached). We can support your ask but want to be transparent on operational trade-offs. Proposed path: 

1) Short-term (<= 7 business days): Ops manual pin + add route config flags (allow_fallback=false, enforce_region=eu). This will be a deployment-level setting we flip for your account. During this window, you may see higher rejection rates if traffic exceeds provisioned capacity.

2) Medium-term (4–6 weeks): Engineering implements non-elastic pinned model routing and reserved capacity recommendation. This reduces risk and improves predictability. We will provide a cost estimate for reserved capacity in the RFC.

Next steps: I’ll send a one-page note summarizing the above and a draft contract clause for Legal to review. Can Medisys confirm if they can accept a short-term SLA exception and/or provide a committed capacity number? If you can share expected peak RPS and percent tail tolerance, our capacity estimate will be faster.

Thanks — I’ll attach the Exec summary and next steps once I have the numbers from Eng.

— Camila
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference

Attachments: medisys-eu-requirements.xlsx
